newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auckland targets 35/65 ratio.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auckland targets 35/65 ratio.

text.p: Ports of Auckland Ltd is targetting a debt-equity ratio of 35:65 following the payment of its special dividend of 30 cents per share for the June year, the chairman, Sir Richard Carter, said on Tuesday.

"We have indicated previously that a suitable target is to have a debt to equity ratio of 35:65. We have a commercial loan facility in place on excellent terms which will enable us to raise further debt when we require," Carter told a briefing of analysts and journalists.
In the year to June, Ports of Auckland will pay NZ$23.9 million in ordinary dividends - the same as last year.
The special dividend will add NZ$39.7 million to the total.
Chief executive Goeff Vazey said container volumes continued to outstrip national growth. They rose 15 percent to a total of 464,000 TEUs (twenty foot equivalent units) over the June year.

Volume of dairy products through Auckland rose 36 percent to 535,000 tonnes, reflecting a strong year for dairy prices. Dairy product exports were changing from pallets to containers, which helped attract volume to Auckland.
"The dairy industry is forecasting a steady year ahead and we are confident that we should be able to retain our market share," Vazey said.
Meat volumes increased by nine percent to nearly 226,000 tonnes.
There was a 30 percent increase in timber and wood exports through Auckland, to 138,000 tonnes.
Pulp and paper was down slightly in the year, but was growing strongly, aided in part by Carter Holt Harvey Ltd's export drive.
There was strong growth in used car imports, up 24 percent on the previous year, while volumes of new built-up cars dropped slightly overall.
Vazey said the recent customs department crackdown on imports would result in a fall a volumes but the decline was expected to be temporary.
Ports of Auckland stock closed at NZ$7.40, up 25 cents from Monday's close.
